subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Edexcel spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Edexcel Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: What is the denary (decimal) value of the 8-bit binary number 00101101?
questions.explain: Place values with a 1 are 32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 45. The set bits are at columns 32, 8, 4 and 1.

questions.q: What is the denary number 200 as an 8-bit binary number?
What is the hexadecimal value of the binary number 11110000?
options: FF
F0
0A
0F
questions.explain: Split into nibbles: 1111 = F and 0000 = 0, giving F0. A common error is reversing the nibbles to 0F.

questions.q: What is the denary value of the hexadecimal number 2A?
questions.explain: 2A = (2 x 16) + (10) = 32 + 10 = 42, because the hex digit A represents 10.

questions.q: Why is hexadecimal often used by programmers instead of long binary numbers?
options: Hex is shorter and easier for humans to read, and each hex digit maps to exactly 4 binary bits
Hexadecimal can represent decimals that binary cannot
Computers store data directly in hexadecimal
Hex uses only the digits 0 and 1
questions.explain: Each hex digit maps to exactly one nibble (4 bits), so hex is a compact, human-readable shorthand for binary. Computers still store data in binary.

questions.q: What is the result of the binary addition 00110101 + 00010011?
questions.explain: 00110101 = 53 and 00010011 = 19; 53 + 19 = 72 = 01001000. You can also add column by column, carrying where two 1s meet.

questions.q: When adding two 8-bit binary numbers, what happens if the result needs a 9th bit that cannot be stored?
options: The number is automatically rounded down
The computer converts the result to denary
The extra bit is stored in hexadecimal
An overflow error occurs because the result is too large for 8 bits
questions.explain: If a carry goes beyond the most significant bit and there is no room, an overflow occurs - the result is too large to be represented in the available number of bits.

questions.q: The binary number 00000110 is shifted left by 2 places. What is the result, and what has happened to its value?
options: 00000001, value divided by 4
00110000, value multiplied by 8
00001100, value multiplied by 2
00011000, value multiplied by 4
questions.explain: 00000110 = 6. Shifting left 2 places gives 00011000 = 24, which is 6 x 4. A left shift of n places multiplies by 2 to the power n.

questions.q: The binary number 00011000 is shifted right by 1 place. What effect does this have on its denary value?
options: It multiplies the value by 2
It subtracts 1 from the value
It leaves the value unchanged
It divides the value by 2
questions.explain: A right shift of 1 place divides by 2. 00011000 = 24 becomes 00001100 = 12. A common mistake is confusing left (multiply) and right (divide) shifts.

questions.q: Using 8-bit two's complement, what is the denary value of 11111100?
questions.explain: The leading 1 means it is negative. Invert to 00000011 and add 1 to get 00000100 = 4, so the value is -4. (Or 256 - 252 = 4, giving -4.)

questions.q: What is -5 represented as an 8-bit two's complement binary number?
questions.explain: Start with +5 = 00000101, invert to 11111010, then add 1 to get 11111011. 00000101 would be +5, not -5.

questions.q: In an 8-bit two's complement number, what does the most significant (leftmost) bit indicate?
options: The number of bytes used
The sign of the number: 0 for positive, 1 for negative
Whether the number is odd or even
Whether the number should be shifted
questions.explain: In two's complement the most significant bit is the sign bit: 0 indicates a positive value and 1 indicates a negative value.

questions.q: Standard ASCII uses 7 bits per character. How many different characters can it represent?
questions.explain: 7 bits give 2 to the power 7 = 128 possible characters (codes 0-127). A common error is answering 256, which is 8 bits.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of Unicode over standard ASCII?
options: It can represent characters from many more languages and symbols, including emoji
It stores images as well as text
It does not require any bits to store a character
It uses fewer bits per character so files are always smaller
questions.explain: Unicode uses more bits per character, allowing it to represent a far larger character set covering many world languages and symbols, unlike ASCII's 128 characters.

questions.q: In ASCII the character 'A' has code 65. What is the ASCII code for the character 'C'?
questions.explain: Uppercase letters are sequential, so A=65, B=66, C=67. Code 97 is lowercase 'a'.

questions.q: A bitmap image is 100 pixels wide, 50 pixels high, with a colour depth of 3 bits per pixel. What is the file size in bits (ignoring metadata)?
options: 15000 bits
1875 bits
150 bits
5000 bits
questions.explain: File size in bits = width x height x colour depth = 100 x 50 x 3 = 15000 bits.

questions.q: What does increasing the colour depth of a bitmap image do?
options: Has no effect on file size
Reduces the number of colours available and shrinks the file
Increases the number of colours that can be represented but increases the file size
Only changes the width of the image
questions.explain: Colour depth is the number of bits per pixel; a depth of n bits gives 2 to the power n colours. More colours mean a larger file size.

questions.q: What is meant by the sample rate when digitising sound?
options: The number of samples taken of the analogue signal per second
The number of speakers used to play the sound
The number of bits used to store each sample
The total length of the sound in seconds
questions.explain: Sample rate is the number of samples captured per second (measured in Hz). Bits per sample is the sample resolution (bit depth), a separate factor.

questions.q: Using the units in the Edexcel specification, how many bytes are in one kibibyte (KiB)?
options: 1000 bytes
8 bytes
512 bytes
1024 bytes
questions.explain: The Edexcel spec uses binary prefixes: 1 kibibyte (KiB) = 1024 bytes, 1 mebibyte (MiB) = 1024 KiB, and so on. A byte is 8 bits.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between lossy and lossless compression?
options: Both permanently remove data equally
Lossy keeps all original data; lossless permanently removes data
Lossless always produces smaller files than lossy
Lossy permanently removes some data to reduce file size; lossless reduces size while allowing the original to be fully restored
questions.explain: Lossy compression discards data that is less noticeable to reduce file size and cannot be reversed exactly. Lossless compression reduces size without losing any data, so the original can be perfectly reconstructed.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Computer Science (1CP2) specification; Data Representation
